question.:question/problem: Which of the following is a lower triangular matrix?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that $B$ is a matrix for which all entries *above* the diagonal are $0$'s:

$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & 10\end{bmatrix}
$$

Hence, it is a lower triangular matrix. 

By contrast, matrices $A$, $C$, $D$, and $E$ each have at least one non-zero entry above the diagonal:

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}4 & 5 \\ 0 & -7\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
C=\begin{bmatrix}6 & 2 \\ 0 & 5\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
D=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 5 \\ 0 & 9\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
E=\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 9 \\ -5 & -10\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, they are not lower triangular matrices.
